title: With Due Respect (Vol. 1) -- Ch. 5: Country, Democracy, and Economy
keywords: Catholic Bishops' Conference of the Philippines
primary_topics: Chapter 5 of 'With Due Respect' (Vol. 1) -- CJP's March 23, 2008 Inquirer column responding to GMA's Lenten vow to eradicate corruption and to the CBCP's diagnosis of a 'crisis of truth and the pervading cancer of corruption'

His restatement of the issues-not-persons creed -- 'I am not for or against GMA... I am for saving our country, our democracy, and our economy. Through methods that are constitutional, moral, and rational' -- distilled into the slogan 'Por la patria, not por la Gloria'

The conditional case for letting GMA finish her term: if she halts Charter change, ensures an honest 2010 transfer, fights graft (prosecuting 'biggies,' naming an independent COA chair), appoints trustworthy justices, and heeds the CBCP and the WPA, 'then she deserves to finish her term'

A point-by-point manifesto of what CJP stands for (an untrammeled pursuit of truth, a peaceful 2010 transfer, the primacy of the Constitution and human rights, strengthened institutions, leadership by example, and 'liberty and prosperity under the rule of law') and what he is against (any pre-2010 Charter revision and any forceful power grab)
sub_topics: The occasion: GMA's Lenten Message vowing again to eradicate corruption, in obvious response to the CBCP's pastoral statement on 'a crisis of truth and the pervading cancer of corruption'

The Watch, Pray and Act (WPA) Movement -- leaders of the nation's Catholic schools -- committing, per the CBCP's call 'to pray together, reason together, decide together, and act together,' to a point-by-point program for 'truth, accountability, and reform'

CJP's recap of his recent columns: challenging citizens to rage for truth while advising GMA she could save her presidency by credibly promising to relinquish power on June 30, 2010 and to abate corruption immediately; he had urged her to waive executive privilege and let Neri testify (a call Brother Mike Velarde joined)

The recurring reader question -- 'Are you for or against GMA?' -- and his answer: trained as a jurist to be 'for or against issues and principles, not for or against personalities,' he is 'for saving our country, our democracy, and our economy' through constitutional, moral and rational methods

The conditional bargain: if GMA abandons Charter change, assures an honest and peaceful 2010 transfer, sincerely fights graft (prosecuting some 'biggies' and naming an independent COA chair), and appoints trustworthy justices to the 2009 vacancies, 'then she deserves to finish her term' -- and the citizens may keep flexing their constitutional rights to hold her to it

Her own culpability deferred: there will be 'enough time for that after she relinquishes the presidency'; Salonga has already filed a complaint with the Ombudsman, and a vigilant citizenry and strengthened institutions will let 'justice take its natural course'

The affirmative manifesto: a 'determined and relentless' pursuit of truth and abatement of corruption; a peaceful 2010 transfer to her constitutional successor; the precedence of the Constitution, rule of law and human rights; the strengthening of institutions (the Court, Comelec, COA, Civil Service Commission and Ombudsman); principled, visionary leadership by example; the primacy of integrity, accountability and transparency; promotion of the economy and the OFWs; and 'the safeguarding of liberty and the nurturance of prosperity under the rule of law'

The negative manifesto: against any pre-2010 Charter revision 'for any purpose and by any method' (always suspect as a cover to extend her stay), and against any 'forceful power grab' (coup, emergency rule, martial law, military takeover, rebellion or secession) -- while conceding peaceful means (election, impeachment, people power) as legitimate though unlikely soon

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 5 of 'With Due Respect' (Vol. 1), CJP's March 23, 2008 Inquirer column, responds to GMA's Lenten vow to eradicate corruption and to the CBCP's diagnosis of 'a crisis of truth and the pervading cancer of corruption,' which the Catholic schools' Watch, Pray and Act (WPA) Movement answered with a program for 'truth, accountability, and reform.' Addressing the recurring reader question -- 'Are you for or against GMA?' -- he restates his creed: as a jurist he is 'for or against issues and principles, not... personalities,' and is 'for saving our country, our democracy, and our economy. Through methods that are constitutional, moral, and rational,' crystallized in the slogan 'Por la patria, not por la Gloria.' He offers a conditional bargain: if GMA abandons Charter change, assures an honest and peaceful 2010 transfer, sincerely fights graft (prosecuting some 'biggies,' naming an independent COA chair, appointing trustworthy justices to the 2009 vacancies) and heeds the CBCP and WPA, 'then she deserves to finish her term' -- with her own culpability to be addressed afterward, where Salonga's Ombudsman complaint already awaits and 'justice will take its natural course.' He then sets out an explicit manifesto: he stands for an untrammeled pursuit of truth and abatement of corruption, a peaceful constitutional transfer by June 30, 2010, the precedence of the Constitution, rule of law and human rights, the strengthening of institutions (Court, Comelec, COA, Civil Service Commission and Ombudsman), principled visionary leadership by example, the primacy of integrity, accountability and transparency, the promotion of the economy and the OFWs, and 'the safeguarding of liberty and the nurturance of prosperity under the rule of law' -- and he stands against any pre-2010 Charter revision 'for any purpose and by any method' and any 'forceful power grab,' while conceding peaceful means as legitimate though unlikely in the near term.
